Design references · retained and expanded

Official studio projects · original work and credits

Liberty ↗Pentagram · Harry Pearce

Purple, black, and white anchor the identity. 13 Plum borrows the deep-purple/neutral relationship, using a grayer purple for tool interfaces.

 Plenaire ↗Pentagram · Jody Hudson-Powell / Luke Powell

Lightness, negative space, and restrained accents. 14 Slate borrows that low visual weight; blue-gray was chosen separately for Keysy.

 The Wing ↗Pentagram · Emily Oberman

Pink paired with deep navy, inspired by stationery. 15 Navy / Rose uses navy for structure and pink for small accents.

 deZaan ↗Pentagram · Angus Hyland's team

Warm/cool relationships between blue, black/white, and copper. 16 Cocoa / Ice is Keysy's interpretation: deep cocoa structure with ice-blue selection and dark-mode accents.

 ERM ↗Pentagram · Marina Willer's team

Layers of light/dark greens and neutrals. The retired 17 Pine / Chalk reduces saturation, pairing near-black pine and pale gray-green for steady reading.

 Cohere ↗Pentagram · Jody Hudson-Powell / Luke Powell

Natural neutrals alongside artificial hues. The retired 18 Aubergine / Celadon extends that two-color relationship; the reference is the design team's work, with separately composed values.

 Shop ↗PORTO ROCHA · Felipe Rocha / Leo Porto
Design: Nathan Fyock / Rachel Quan / Luis Alejandro

Warm black and gray-white support purple. 19 Ink / Iris strengthens the accent while keeping the interface clear with a single solid color.

Palettes 13–19 were composed for Keysy, not copied from reference brand colors. This round originally compared 16 Cocoa / Ice × 33 Fit with 18 Aubergine / Celadon × 34 Custody; palette 18 has since been removed.
